source.version_note: Frontiers in Psychology, Methods article, volume 7, article 1717, published 2 November 2016; received 22 June and accepted 18 October 2016.
source.verification_method: All five supplied pages and all 16 references read. Both loading tables and the two-panel seven-target Figure 1 visually inspected. Crossref verifies main identity, three authors and publication date, and the identity of the cited Moriguchi 2015 item. No respondent-level data, analysis code, original 2007/2014 questionnaires or cited book independently fully reviewed.

citation.title: Semantic Differential Scale Method Can Reveal Multi-Dimensional Aspects of Mind Perception

reading.source_scope_note: One Japanese online self-report measurement comparison, N=500, rating seven named targets on two questionnaires. PCA and correlations concern attributed capacities and impressions, not actual AI mentality, a new psychological mechanism, a clinical validation or a randomized test removing prior knowledge.
access_limits: No respondent-level data, analysis code, covariance matrix, response/exclusion flow, factor-score computation or complete covariance-adjusted correlation output supplied in this file. Exact analysis units and dependence handling are not sufficiently specified for reproduction.

Original Gray 2007, Takahashi 2014, Harvey book and cited cross-cultural/clinical studies are not independently fully read or credited from their references. The 2014 N=20 and original Gray >2000 are separate cited samples, not extra participants in this study.

No live robots, target pictures, clinical patients, prospective outcomes, longitudinal follow-up or cross-cultural comparison were tested here. Figure icons depict target labels, not experimental visual stimuli.

study.sample: 500 Japanese respondents recruited through Cross Marketing, described as healthy, ages 17–75, mean 45.0, SD18.9, with age quotas and equal gender proportions. The health-screening method, invitation denominator, response rate, missingness and exclusions are not detailed. Age/gender balance does not establish population representativeness.
study.ethics: Written informed consent and Declaration of Helsinki compliance are stated. The supplied text does not identify a review board or protocol number; do not invent an approval or infer misconduct from this reporting limit.
study.targets: Each respondent rates an adult friend, baby, frog, tree, communication robot, supercomputer and god. Targets are presented as words only, in randomized target order. Which questionnaire comes first, adjective-direction counterbalancing and exact participant burden effects are not specified.
study.measures: Gray-style questionnaire: 18 mental-capacity items, five-point suitability ratings. Takahashi-style semantic differential: 21 opposing adjective pairs, seven-point ratings. Both are verbal explicit self-reports. Adjective ratings do not become implicit measures, direct neural evidence or knowledge-free intuition merely by avoiding hunger-type capacity questions.
study.capacity_pca: Two components above eigenvalue 1: 11.4 (63.4% variance) and 2.2 (12.3%), labeled experience and agency. All 18 items load positively on the first component, including planning/morality; the second contrasts positive planning/memory-like loadings with negative hunger/pain-like loadings. Factor signs are arbitrary; negative loadings do not mean negative subjective capacity or proof of no mind.
study.adjective_pca: Three components are reported, not only two: 11.6 (55.1%), 3.0 (14.3%) and approximately1.0 (4.9%). The first two are labeled emotion/intelligence. The third is omitted from discussion because it is not significantly correlated with the Gray dimensions. Its rounded eigenvalue of1.0 is not proof that the over1.0 rule was violated; unrounded values are unavailable.
study.construct_boundary: The first adjective component also loads on nice, positive, active and long-sighted, while the second includes ethical, responsible and emotionally stable. Labels are interpretations of covariance, not pure emotion/intelligence measurements. Orthogonal PCA components are a mathematical property, not proof that human psychological dimensions are naturally independent.
study.convergence: Reported correspondences are experience–emotion r=.80 and agency–intelligence r=.75, both p<.00001. The second pair is mislabeled in the printed parenthesis. A correlation supports overlap but not interchangeability, measurement invariance, superior validity or causal removal of prior knowledge.
study.dependence: Seven targets are rated repeatedly by the same500 respondents. The paper does not clearly specify whether correlation/PCA observations are participant-target scores, participant aggregates or target aggregates, or how repeated-person and repeated-target dependence is handled. Do not infer an independent sample of3500, silently reconstruct a p-value from seven target means or assert a calculation is definitely wrong without the analysis unit.
study.figure: Both panels plot target means without uncertainty intervals. Robot/supercomputer are high on the labeled agency/intelligence axis, adult friend is high on experience/emotion, and baby is low on agency/intelligence. These are positions in relative component space, not measured machine intelligence, sentience or within-person superiority in every respondent.
study.age_nulls: The authors report no significant age correlations in any target/dimension, without coefficients or intervals. This is not equivalence or proof that age, cohort or cultural exposure never matters.
study.culture: Japanese-versus-Western explanations compare this sample with earlier studies differing in target sets, instruments and context. No country/culture randomization or measurement-invariance test isolates a cultural effect. Religious generalizations and universal cross-cultural validity claims extend beyond the observed sample.
study.clinical_and_social_benefits: Possible use for psychiatric assessment and improved human–robot rapport/trust is proposed or cited secondarily. The study does not test diagnostic accuracy, clinical sensitivity/specificity, actual trust behavior, safety or causal empathy effects.
study.interpretive_contrast: Distinguishing spontaneous impressions from explicit knowledge is a useful research question. Replacing capacity items with adjectives changes content, response scales and construct coverage simultaneously; this comparison does not uniquely demonstrate that a prior-knowledge bias was removed.

summary: No new entries. Enrich agency attribution, experience attribution and anthropomorphism with a direct, limited questionnaire comparison, and animism with an explicitly secondary cultural definition. Correct the duplicated correlation-pair label and table-instrument attribution, retain three-component and repeated-measures caveats, and flag an unresolved citation-to-claim mismatch without inventing a replacement.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity a capacity for intentional thought, planning and action.
findings.novelty_rationale: The concept already exists; add a direct measurement comparison or a clearly marked secondary definition rather than a new label.

evidence.quote: the dimension of “agency” indicates the capacity to plan

findings.evidence_scope: N=500 Japanese respondents rate seven word-labeled targets. A Gray-style agency component correlates r=.75 with the adjective-scale intelligence component; the robot/supercomputer target means lie high on the relative second axis. This is perceived agency measurement, not actual capability.
findings.boundary: Both questionnaires are explicit self-reports, and component labels/signs are not direct psychological mechanisms. Relative component positions do not establish sentience, moral agency, machine superiority or a knowledge-free scale. Correlation units/dependence and invariance require further information.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity the capacity for subjective feelings or sensations, such as pleasure, pain, fear or joy.
findings.novelty_rationale: The concept already exists; add a direct measurement comparison or a clearly marked secondary definition rather than a new label.

evidence.quote: the capacity to sense and feel emotions,

findings.evidence_scope: The Gray-style experience component correlates r=.80 with the semantic-differential emotion component. This supports some convergence between capacity judgments and adjective impressions in this sample, while content and response formats differ.
findings.boundary: Perceived feelings differ from actual subjective experience. A positive first component also includes cognitive items, so it cannot be assumed a pure feeling factor. Neither association nor a null age test establishes equivalence, clinical validity or universal structure.

findings.definition: Attributing human characteristics, intentions, emotions or other mental states to a nonhuman entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: The concept already exists; add a direct measurement comparison or a clearly marked secondary definition rather than a new label.

evidence.quote: attributing minds to inanimate agents improves trustworthiness

findings.evidence_scope: The paper motivates measuring impressions of artificial targets and compares two questionnaires. It cites earlier trust/empathy findings as background; no trust or empathy effect is newly tested. Target labels alone, rather than live humanlike behavior, generate the present ratings.
findings.boundary: Humanlike appearance, attributed mind, prior knowledge, warmth and actual reliability are distinct. The present measurement comparison does not show that anthropomorphism causes warranted trust, improves safety or licenses misleading users about machine capacities.

findings.definition: Attributing life, vitality or a soul to nonhuman entities, including objects or features of nature.
findings.novelty_rationale: The concept already exists; add a direct measurement comparison or a clearly marked secondary definition rather than a new label.

evidence.quote: Animism is the cultural attitude toward nature

findings.evidence_scope: The discussion describes beliefs that minds may be attributed to nonliving entities as animism, with Harvey2005 cited secondarily. This overlaps the retained animism entry and motivates measurement questions; it is not a cross-cultural or developmental animism experiment.
findings.boundary: Attributing mind, life or spirit need not involve projecting a specifically human personality. No uniform Japanese/Christian belief, literal soul, pathology or verified machine experience follows from a target rating. The cited book is not an independently read source in this review.

source_corrections.correction: The preceding sentence and stated comparison identify the second pair as agency–intelligence. Preserve the reported r=.75 while correcting the duplicated pair label; do not invent a different coefficient or claim to reproduce it from unavailable respondent data.
source_corrections.scope: Internal text/context and visual page check.

source_corrections.reported: Two components in Takahashi et al.,2014, above the18 mental-capacity items.
source_corrections.correction: Methods/Results identify these as the Gray2007-style capacity items used in the current survey; the21 adjective pairs belong to Takahashi2014-style measurement. Label the instrument and current analysis separately so the current500-person results are not mistaken for the prior20-person study.
source_corrections.scope: Instrument attribution within the fully read paper; original2007/2014 datasets not independently reviewed.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.location: PDF page4 child/stuffed-animal statement and page5 Moriguchi2015 reference
unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: The cited DOI10.3389/fpsyg.2015.00894 is Teaching others rule-use improves executive function and prefrontal activations in young children, verified by Crossref. Its identity does not directly identify a stuffed-animal friendship study. Check the exact supporting passage before using this as evidence; no replacement paper is asserted and the original was not independently fully read.

No clearly defined correlation observation unit, full target-level/individual score output or dependence correction is supplied. The reported tiny p-values cannot be checked by assuming seven plotted means are the inferential sample.

methodological_limits: One age/gender-balanced online Japanese sample; cross-cultural, age-equivalence and clinical generalization unsupported by this design alone.
Two explicit rating methods differ in items and scales. Convergence does not uniquely show elimination of prior knowledge or superior measurement validity.
PCA dimension names and orthogonality are not direct mental mechanisms; third component exists and factor signs are arbitrary.
Repeated targets/respondents, unclear inferential units and missing raw data/code prevent full statistical reproduction. Target mean diagrams lack uncertainty intervals.

cross_paper_learning.finding: The later live-action progress report raises similar concerns about capacity wording and implicit/explicit measures. This completed questionnaire comparison supplies correlations, but does not validate the later IAT, its generation effects or its still-unreported outcomes.

As in the healthcare factor analysis, loading sign is arbitrary and a first general-positive component should not be treated as a uniquely pure psychological capacity. Distinguish PCA convergence from separate CFA, invariance and clinical validation.
The embodied/disembodied distinction matters: target names and subjective rating instruments here do not reproduce live robot interaction, neural mentalizing or actual machine experience.

deferred.reason: Measurement labels and instrument, overlapping retained attribution constructs, not new independent behaviors.
Names from a cited2014 study without sufficient distinct definitions here. Read that original before creating rows.
Motivating distinction and cross-study hypothesis, not a uniquely isolated new behavioral effect or controlled cultural comparison.

limitations: No new entries, independent credits for unread books/cited studies, invented annual counts, automatic ethical/harm edges, clinical diagnosis or proof of actual machine mentality.
